Subject: Post-call: LumaHealth — model fit, performance profiles & next steps

Hi Alice — great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our call and the immediate next steps we discussed: 

- High-level read: your primary concerns are throughput on the inference path (peak TPS during clinic hours), latency tail for patient-facing chat, and minimizing hallucinations on medication instructions.
- We ran a short baseline on your sample prompt set (thank you for sharing the CSV) and have Redwood-verified performance profiles attached.
- Proposed next steps: (1) run a 24-hour eval with your full prompt set on the recommended model variant, (2) workshop on prompt edits and safety filters, (3) propose a 2-week canary on Dedicated capacity to validate production metrics.

Attachments: redwood_verified_profiles_20260310.csv, customer_prompt_set_luma_v1.md (prompt excerpt you provided).

I called out three candidate model configurations that balance cost and quality for the workflows you described: 

1) redwood-small-1.1 (int8) — recommended for routing conversational notifications and short replies where cost and higher TPS matter. Redwood-verified: 120 TPS (p95 latency 85 ms, p99 210 ms) on our 8xA100 benchmark. Quality tradeoff: slightly lower factuality on long medication descriptions.

2) redwood-13b-q4f-optimized — good middle ground for chat assistants that need better context management. Redwood-verified: 45 TPS (p95 160 ms, p99 420 ms). Better coherence on multi-step instructions.

3) redwood-70b-quant-mixed — highest quality for clinical instructions and summarization (recommended for any path that writes medication instructions). Redwood-verified: 12 TPS (p95 380 ms, p99 940 ms) on similar sequence lengths.

Links: Redwood console perf page: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/LUMA-20260310 (has raw trace + latency percentiles). Also shared a Drive folder with the raw CSVs and the prompt set we used: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Redwood-LUMA-benchmarks

Open questions we need to close to size a Dedicated pool and finalize the quote: 
- Peak concurrent requests per minute during 09:00–12:00 PT?
- Typical sequence length for full conversation (tokens) vs. notification payloads?
- PII handling: are any messages subject to regional data residency?

Proposed timeline: I can schedule the 24-hour eval as soon as we get the full prompt corpus (we used the excerpt you shared). If that looks good, we’ll run the canary next week and present a short summary + recommendation.

Would you be available for a 30-minute workshop Thursday morning to go over the prompt edits?

Thanks,
Soojin
